5vd842:250: Agent Trace is fundamentally different from traditional Trace. Traditional Trace (e.g., OpenTelemetry) records service call chains — a single request lasts from seconds to minutes, the Schema is stable, and the analysis focuses on Latency, Status, and Error. Agent Trace, by contrast, is characterized by: long spans (tasks lasting from tens of minutes to hours), large JSON (a single Trace ranging from 500KB to 500MB), and dirty data (LLM outputs are often not valid JSON). A single task in an Agent Swarm can produce 500MB of data and 100,000+ Spans.
5xqmp9:218: Zhang Yanfei's "Trace as Evals" is essentially a reconstruction of Agent observability and evaluation systems. The traditional evaluation approach is "execute first, evaluate later" — after the Agent finishes a task, an independent Eval dataset is used to judge whether the result is good or bad. But an Agent is a non-deterministic system: LLMs hallucinate, and the same task with the same input executed at different times can produce completely different results. This means evaluation methods that "only look at the final result" cannot locate the root cause of problems — you don't know whether the Prompt is at fault, the Tool selection was wrong, or the context had key information trimmed away.
c35syl:30: Make the Trace system the first priority in Agent infrastructure.
fm13ue:214: The talk outlined the three-stage evolution of "Prompt Engineering → Context Engineering → Harness Engineering," mapping a clear trajectory for AI Agent engineering. The first stage (2023-2024) optimized the input text of single model calls; the second stage (2024-2025) managed the information flow in multi-turn interactions (RAG, memory, context window scheduling); the third stage (2025-present) addresses autonomous task execution by Agents and multi-Agent collaboration.

jgrh7n:239: Databend's solution offers strong engineering reference value: building a minimal Trace foundation based on object storage + VARIANT type + acceleration columns + full-text search + Stream/Task. The core idea is to "land the data first" — retain raw Traces long-term, and don't only look at the final Pass/Fail. Then, leveraging the database's JSON acceleration columns, full-text indexing, and incremental aggregation capabilities, multiple higher-level capabilities such as Eval, Replay, and RL are built on the same data. This architecture of "one data source serving multiple scenarios" is simpler and more economical than building separate storage for each scenario.

kvp2hi:188: The breakthrough of "Trace as Evals" lies in building evaluation directly into the execution process itself. The complete trace produced by every Agent execution — including each step's System Prompt, tool descriptions, Tool Call sequences, execution results, Token consumption, and time overhead — is itself the most authentic evaluation data. Evaluation is no longer a "post-hoc checklist" but a "comprehensive audit of the execution process." This paradigm shift makes it possible to upgrade from "judging whether results are right or wrong" to "analyzing process quality."
